m3-t1.introduction: A second way to understand “Recruitment funnels and source performance”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: A cohort and a period report are not the same funnel
sections.explanation: A cohort follows the same eligible applications. Period event totals may describe different applications at different stages.

items.label: Cohort entry
items.detail: Define which applications enter and when.

items.label: Observation boundary
items.detail: State the cut-off and treatment of open cases.

items.label: Period events
items.detail: Count events in an interval without assuming shared membership.

items.label: Comparability
items.detail: Align maturity and scope before comparing cohorts.

sections.takeaway: Do not divide unrelated event flows and call the result a cohort conversion rate.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Choose a cohort or a period flow

sections.title: Follow the mature application cohort
sections.explanation: The practice fixture follows the same 24 synthetic applications through nested stages. Each conversion uses its own eligible previous-stage count.

items.label: Applications
items.detail: The eligible entry cohort; not a count of unrelated calendar-period events.

items.label: Screen passed
items.detail: 18 of 24 reached this stage.

items.label: Interviewed
items.detail: 16 of the 18 screen passes were interviewed.

items.label: Offers
items.detail: 12 of the 16 interviewed applications received offers.

items.label: Accepted
items.detail: 9 of 12 offers were accepted.

items.label: Joined
items.detail: 7 of 9 accepted offers became joins by the observation boundary.

sections.takeaway: Offer acceptance is 9/12 = 75%; application-to-join yield is 7/24 ≈ 29.17%. They answer different questions.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Cost per joined hire needs matched scope
sections.explanation: The mature synthetic fixture allocates ₹40,000 to Source A and ₹36,000 to Source B, with four and three joined hires respectively.

items.label: Source A
items.detail: ₹40,000 ÷ 4 joined hires; 12 applications in the source cohort.

items.label: Source B
items.detail: ₹36,000 ÷ 3 joined hires; 12 applications in the source cohort.

sections.takeaway: These small simplified cohorts do not establish source quality or causality. Also review role mix, access, timing and selection evidence.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Can 12 offers issued this month be divided by 24 unrelated applications received this month to establish cohort conversion?
checkpoint.answer: No. The events may involve different applications. Use a matched cohort with a clear observation boundary, or label the figures as separate period flows.

m3-t2.introduction: A second way to understand “Time-to-fill, time-to-hire and recruitment cost”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Different clocks answer different recruitment questions
sections.explanation: This course defines the event boundaries explicitly. Other organisations may use another convention, which must be disclosed.

items.label: Time-to-fill
items.detail: Requisition approval to accepted offer; elapsed calendar days excluding the start day.

items.label: Time-to-hire
items.detail: Candidate application to accepted offer under the same calendar convention.

items.label: Joining lag
items.detail: Accepted offer to joining is a separate interval.

items.label: Open age
items.detail: Elapsed time so far for unfinished work, reported separately.

sections.takeaway: An open requisition has an age, not a completed zero-day fill duration.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Name the start and end events

sections.title: A cost metric needs a declared inclusion rule
sections.explanation: Costs can arise before a hire and may be allocated differently. Match the numerator and denominator using an agreed period or cohort.

items.label: Define costs
items.detail: State included internal and external costs and currency.

items.label: Match attribution
items.detail: Align the costs with the hires they support.

items.label: Check the denominator
items.detail: Specify whether hires means accepted or actually joined.

items.label: Explain exclusions
items.detail: Document allocations, limits and comparison context.

sections.takeaway: Lower cost per hire alone does not prove better hiring quality or fair access.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Locate the delay before judging a person
sections.explanation: The overall duration combines different stages and constraints, including role difficulty and stakeholder availability.

items.label: Inspect timestamps
items.detail: Check event validity and missing coverage.

items.label: Split the process
items.detail: Identify approval, scheduling, feedback and offer waits.

items.label: Compare like roles
items.detail: Review distributions and unusual legitimate cases.

items.label: Test an improvement
items.detail: Assign a bounded process change with balancing measures.

sections.takeaway: Use comparable cases and an authorised process review rather than a simplistic recruiter ranking.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Should an unfilled requisition be assigned a time-to-fill of zero?
checkpoint.answer: No. Its completed duration is unknown. Report open age separately and keep it visible rather than making unfinished work look faster.

m3-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Structured selection and candidate experience”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: A selection score needs job-related evidence
sections.explanation: A structured scorecard links an actual role requirement to observable evidence. A numeric label does not automatically make judgement objective.

items.label: Define the work
items.detail: Identify the role’s actual tasks and essential competencies.

items.label: Specify anchors
items.detail: Describe observable evidence at each relevant level.

items.label: Collect consistently
items.detail: Use appropriate core questions and work samples.

items.label: Review fairly
items.detail: Inspect context, accessibility and human judgement.

sections.takeaway: Use the authorised HR process for accommodations and avoid unsupported personal or automated ranking.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Calibrate meaning without forcing agreement
sections.explanation: Independent notes preserve evidence before a group discussion. Calibration clarifies the standard rather than demanding identical scores.

items.label: Record first
items.detail: Write evidence independently against the agreed anchors.

items.label: Compare judgements
items.detail: Identify where interpretations differ materially.

items.label: Discuss the evidence
items.detail: Use role requirements instead of seniority or personal impressions.

items.label: Document the conclusion
items.detail: Retain the reason and any unresolved limitation.

sections.takeaway: Do not infer sensitive characteristics from a name, photograph or social-media proxy.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Candidate feedback is not selection evidence
sections.explanation: Voluntary process feedback can reveal communication problems, but respondents may differ from people who did not reply.

items.label: Define a measure
items.detail: State eligible invitations, responses and period.

items.label: Collect safely
items.detail: Explain purpose and protect appropriate confidentiality.

items.label: Interpret cautiously
items.detail: Keep nonresponse and small samples visible.

items.label: Improve the process
items.detail: Test clearer updates or accessible instructions with an owner.

sections.takeaway: Do not penalise criticism or publish identifiable comments; keep selection and feedback uses separate.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Does giving every candidate a numeric score make a selection process objective?
checkpoint.answer: No. The criteria, anchors, evidence collection and judgement can still be biased or irrelevant. Use job-related structure and authorised human review.

m3-pb2.introduction: A second way to understand “Project Block 2 — Recruitment funnel and selection review”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Recruitment funnel and selection review: connect the question to evidence
sections.explanation: A matched-cohort source comparison with clear cost and duration boundaries and a human-reviewed selection-process recommendation.

items.label: Question
items.detail: A matched-cohort source comparison with clear cost and duration boundaries and a human-reviewed selection-process recommendation.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Use the original practice material with explicit provenance.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Explain a bounded recommendation and the evidence that could change it.

sections.takeaway: The app records reading and quizzes; external project submission, verification and marking remain with the institution.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep synthetic fixtures and authority boundaries separate
sections.explanation: The practice tables are independent examples, not linked real employee records. Use the original inputs and log every deliberate scenario change.

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Identify the fixture, grain, period and original source copy.

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Do not join independent populations as if they were one company dataset.

items.label: Permission
items.detail: Use synthetic inputs and the institution-approved submission route.

items.label: Honest context
items.detail: Do not report simulated interviews, approvals or outcomes as live events.

sections.takeaway: No real personal dataset, paid tool or live organisational access is required or authorised by this project.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reserve time for correction, not only construction
sections.explanation: The original work-plan table supplies the timing. This map groups the work into a review loop without changing those allocations.

items.label: Frame
items.detail: Read the decision and inspect source boundaries.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the required artefacts with traceable formulas or decisions.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Reproduce the headline and inspect assumptions and safeguards.

items.label: Review and revise
items.detail: Use peer or self-review and keep a change log.

items.label: Explain and submit
items.detail: Finish the recommendation, disclosure and evidence index.

sections.takeaway: A first draft is not a finished artefact; retain the comment and your response after review.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Organise the recruitment funnel and selection review submission
sections.explanation: These groups help you locate evidence; the full numbered submission checklist above still defines every required component.

items.label: Funnel
items.detail: Show counts, eligible denominators, observation end and open-case rules.

items.label: Source comparison
items.detail: Keep costs and applications, offers, acceptances and joins aligned.

items.label: Duration examples
items.detail: State start and end events and the calendar convention.

items.label: Structured scorecard
items.detail: Use three job-related competencies with observable anchors.

items.label: Recommendation
items.detail: Address comparability and candidate experience with a bounded pilot.

sections.takeaway: A public portfolio copy must be safe and clearly labelled; it is not a substitute for the editable institutional submission.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Compare matched source costs without a superiority claim
sections.explanation: In the small synthetic fixture, each source has six offers. Source A has five acceptances and four joins; Source B has four acceptances and three joins.

items.label: Source A · ₹10,000 per join
items.detail: Allocated cost ₹40,000 ÷ four joins. Five accepted offers do not make the denominator five.

items.label: Source B · ₹12,000 per join
items.detail: Allocated cost ₹36,000 ÷ three joins. This small comparison does not prove source quality or cause.

sections.takeaway: Keep the denominator as joined hires for this cost comparison. Role mix, access, observation time and selection evidence still constrain interpretation.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Follow the original rubric and its evidence standard
sections.explanation: The original block or capstone marks, performance anchors and institutional award conditions are unchanged.

items.label: Correctness and reproducibility
items.detail: Trace the method and results to the declared source and definitions.

items.label: Judgement and safeguards
items.detail: Show uncertainty, appropriate authority and safe handling.

items.label: Clarity, evidence and reflection
items.detail: Make claims inspectable and explain corrections.

sections.takeaway: These panels and animations do not calculate marks, approve projects or award an external credential.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Review the recommendation from a challenger’s view
sections.explanation: A reviewer should be able to trace a claim, test an assumption and understand which action needs another role’s approval.

items.label: Trace a headline
items.detail: Find the calculation or artefact behind the main claim.

items.label: Challenge an assumption
items.detail: Ask what missing evidence could reverse the action.

items.label: Check authority
items.detail: Name who is permitted to approve a consequential decision.

items.label: Inspect sharing
items.detail: Choose evidence that can safely appear in the public version.

sections.takeaway: Keep the actual review comment and your correction or explanation instead of claiming a review that never happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Explain assistance without outsourcing judgement
sections.explanation: Complete the original AI-use statement even when no AI was used. Tool help must not fabricate records, sources or experience.

items.label: Name tools or none
items.detail: State the actual assistance and permitted synthetic inputs.

items.label: Record your checks
items.detail: Explain accepted, changed and rejected suggestions and independent verification.

items.label: Own the work
items.detail: Describe your contribution, judgement and responsibility for the final claims.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload real employee, candidate, student or credential data to public AI tools; follow exam restrictions separately.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An extension tests an assumption after the core is complete
sections.explanation: The optional extension is not required for full marks. Keep the original work and distinguish a changed scenario from an observation.

items.label: Complete the core
items.detail: Finish the required evidence and safeguards first.

items.label: A changed role mix
items.detail: Compare the recommendation and identify what additional evidence is needed.

items.label: Compare and document
items.detail: Show what changed, which conclusion depends on it and what remains unknown.

sections.takeaway: More complexity does not improve a submission if the reasoning and safeguards cannot be reproduced.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Does Source A’s lower cost per joined hire establish that it is the better source?
checkpoint.answer: No. It is a descriptive result under the declared synthetic cost and cohort boundaries. Review role mix, maturity, access, selection evidence and small-sample uncertainty before making a bounded recommendation.
